title: Scenario: Out of Position on a Dynamic Board

lines.text: Chapter ten, section two. Scenario, out of position on a dynamic board.
Picture a small blind versus big blind confrontation where the small blind three-bet pre-flop.
Flop is queen-jack-ten with two hearts, a highly dynamic board where hand values will keep changing.
The small blind is out of position with a range that is strong but not overwhelmingly ahead.
The big blind's calling range is packed with connected and suited hands that hit this board hard.
In this spot, the small blind's best plan is not to c-bet at high frequency; it is to bet a polarized range with clear value and clear semi-bluff candidates, and check the middle of her range.
Sizing matters: a bigger bet suits the polarized dynamic, and it also compensates for the fact that being out of position makes small stabs vulnerable to floats.

The big blind, meanwhile, should defend a wide calling range against the small stabs but be ready to raise polarized against the big bets, because the small blind's out-of-position range is not big enough to defend against a well-timed raise on a dynamic board.

The general theme is that out-of-position c-betting rewards a polarized shape more than an in-position c-bet does, because the caller's positional advantage can otherwise chew you up on subsequent streets.
